To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the response to chemotherapy is associated with survival benefit and that the response rate is higher in patients with normal serum creatinine values.

(1) alkylating agent based chemotherapy for AL is effective in a subset of the patients and a trial is strongly recommended; (2) the serum creatinine concentration has a negative impact on response rate and (3) patients with nephrototic syndrome, normal serum creatinine, and no echographic evidence of cardiac disease have an excellent response rate.
18% of patients respond to alkylating-agent-based therapy, 78% of patients who respond to therapy survive 5 years or more, and 7% of patients who do not respond to alkylators survive 5 years.
